cases.reason: GR1 governs conversion with the file's alphabets (plural) on every input and output operation of a CODE-SET file. In 2002 those operations include READ/WRITE/REWRITE of an FD whose records carry SELECT WHEN (§2002:13.16.49.3 GR1: SELECT WHEN is evaluated exactly when CODE-SET is specified) and WRITE FILE/REWRITE FILE of an FD with no record description entries (§2002:13.3.4.2 SR3, §2002:13.16.13.3 GR4); both are required in 2002 and both are refused at --std 2002 (COBOL1705, COBOL1706). The reader's evidence (pb793_code_set_ebcdic and single-alphabet identity probes) covers only plain-record, single-alphabet files. §2002:B.3 item 11 does not license the gap: support for CODE-SET is claimed, and §2002:3.1.5 then requires all its functionality. Probes at --std 2002 (identical at 2023): cs-both-selwhen.cob (FD F CODE-SET FOR ALPHANUMERIC IS A1 FOR NATIONAL IS N1, two 01 records with SELECT WHEN IS-A / SELECT WHEN OTHER) -> COBOL1705 on each SELECT WHEN citing §2023 Annex A.4.8, then a cascading COBOL1672 'no SELECT WHEN clauses are specified ... not both' (misleading: they are written), exit 65; cs-both-norec.cob (same CODE-SET, no record description entries, RECORD CONTAINS 8, WRITE FILE F FROM W, READ F INTO W2) -> COBOL1706 citing §2023 Annex A.4.13, exit 65. Both are conforming 2002 programs (§2002:3.1, 3.1.1: only Annex A communications is optional in 2002; SELECT WHEN and WRITE/REWRITE FILE are required 2002 elements).
